Title: Israeli occupiers injure palestinians near jerusalem, seize west bank home
Article:
RAMALLAH: Israeli occupiers injured several Palestinians, including women and elderly people, during an attack late Monday on a Bedouin community near occupied East Jerusalem, while others seized a house under construction and attempted to steal livestock in the occupied West Bank, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
The Jerusalem Governorate said Israeli occupiers backed by Israeli forces attacked residents of the Al-Arara Bedouin community near Jaba, assaulting several Palestinians. It added that Israeli forces prevented ambulance crews from reaching the injured.
The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its teams were initially denied access to the area but later evacuated two Palestinians who sustained injuries in the assault to a hospital in Jaba.
Local sources also said that Israeli occupiers hurled stones at Palestinian vehicles near the Jaba roundabout, damaging several cars. No injuries were reported.
Separately, Israeli forces detained Qusai Ghaith, the son of Jerusalem Governor Adnan Ghaith, after raiding the town of Silwan in occupied East Jerusalem, according to local sources.
The sources said Israeli forces beat Qusai before taking him to a detention and interrogation centre in Jerusalem.
In the central West Bank, Israeli occupiers seized a house under construction belonging to Palestinian resident Ezzedine Tahseen in the village of Deir Ammar west of Ramallah, according to local sources.
In eastern Ramallah, Israeli occupiers stormed a livestock pen belonging to a Palestinian farmer in the village of Burqa and attempted to steal animals before residents forced them to withdraw, the sources added.
Further north, Israeli occupiers opened live fire during an attack on the outskirts of Asira al-Qibliya village south of Nablus before Israeli forces raided the village. No injuries or arrests were reported.
On Friday, Israeli occupiers backed by the army attacked the Palestinian town of Tell near Nablus, killing four Palestinians. Two Israelis were also killed in a shooting during the confrontation, according to Palestinian and Israeli sources.
Israeli forces also imposed a siege on Nablus and surrounding towns following the violence, carried out mass arrest raids, and announced preparations for a wide-scale military operation across the West Bank.
Since Oct 2023, Israeli forces and occupiers have killed at least 1,182 Palestinians in the West Bank, injured thousands and detained around 24,000, according to official Palestinian figures. — BERNAMA

Title: France and Spain race to contain fires before new heatwave
Article:
NAVALUENGA, Spain: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday said one forest fire in southwest France had been "contained" even as another, much bigger one near Bordeaux continued to rage, and western Europe braced for new heatwaves this week.
France and Spain are battling the worst wildfires in living memory, which have ripped through hundreds of hectares of woodland, destroying properties and forcing evacuations of hundreds of thousands of people.
The return of searing temperatures, from Tuesday in France and from Wednesday in Spain, threaten to complicate fire-fighting efforts.
Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said the coming hours would be "absolutely decisive" to bring fires burning west of the capital, Madrid, under control.
Macron, on a visit to a crisis centre in the winemaking capital of Bordeaux, said: "The coming weeks will be tough and we have to hold out."
That southwestern city, in the Gironde region, lies just short distance from a vast and turbulent wildfire that is creating its own winds and sparking fresh blazes around it.
That unchecked, gigantic blaze – which has created a rare pyrocumulonimbus cloud packing lightning – has over the past six days ravaged 42,000 hectares, forced 220,000 people to flee and destroyed 240 houses.
Macron said a smaller fire in the adjoining Landes – which had nonetheless forced the evacuation of more than 30,000 people – was now "contained."
But he warned it "remains virulent and we must be extremely cautious over the next few hours and the coming days."
This was due to the "conditions of climate change in which we will live," he said.
- 'LOST EVERYTHING' -
In Spain, where blazes were burning west of Madrid, some 60,000 people have also been evacuated.
At a sports hall just outside Madrid, displaced people sprawled on camp beds, held their heads in their hands and comforted pets.
Maria Angeles Canete fought back tears as she looked around the desolation that used to be her campsite near Navaluenga, west of the capital.
"We lost everything," she said. "We had this campsite, we had another one, and we've lost it all. We have nothing."
The European Union on Monday announced more water-bombing planes were being sent to France, in addition to those already deployed to Spain.
But EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib told AFP that its fleet was increasingly stretched due to fears they may soon be needed elsewhere.
"Extreme conditions are looming for Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, in addition to France, the Iberian Peninsula... where the situation is expected to worsen, including in Portugal starting today," Lahbib said.
- DEVASTATION -
The scale of the devastation from the fires is vast in the worst-affected areas.
Pine trees smouldered with blackened trunks and smoke rose from charred forests, with the burnt-out husks of cars and houses reduced to shells, AFP reporters said.
"You run to save what you can and then you turn to defend," said Karim Benali, 39, a volunteer firefighter on a road near Navaluenga, in Spain.
That country has seen 77,000 hectares – nearly the size of New York City – destroyed.
David Sanchez, a 48-year-old, had just returned home to Cebreros after evacuating at the weekend to find that his small olive and pistachio grove had been consumed.
"Now it's time to clean up and plant again and that's it...And the fire has flared up again down there," he said, surrounded by choking air that stung the eyes and throat.
Some 150,000 hectares of land have burned in Spain and 115,000 hectares in France since the start of this year.
Earlier this month, 13 people were killed in a wildfire in southwestern Spain while flames ripped through the UNESCO-listed Fontainebleau forest south of Paris.
Near Bordeaux in France, tractors fitted with blades to clear land, pickups towing water tanks and logging trucks sped to join a convoy of fire engines.
"We want to help," said farmer and wood transporter Christopher Bonnefond, 25, in the village of Marcheprime, in the Gironde region.
"I'm a hunter and I want nature to stay like it is."
- CLIMATE CHANGE -
Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called the fires "the most painful expression of a climate emergency."
Spain's weather agency AEMET announced a new heatwave starting Wednesday until the end of the week, with temperatures forecast to hit 42C in the northeast and 39C in the centre.
"The wildfire danger level will continue to increase, reaching extreme levels and making firefighting efforts more difficult due to high temperatures, locally gusty southerly winds and widespread low humidity," AEMET said in a statement.
MeteoFrance also forecast more hot weather of up to 40C from Tuesday with dry wind.--AFP

Title: [WATCH] Fire damages fuel price signboard at BHP petrol station in Kuala Lumpur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A fire broke out at a BHP petrol station along the North-South Expressway near Sungai Besi last night, setting its fuel price signboard ablaze.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said firefighters received an emergency call at 9.57pm before a team from the Seri Kembangan Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene.
"The fire engine arrived at 10.06pm and found that the blaze involved the station's fuel price signboard.
"The fire was brought under control at 10.22pm, and the operation concluded at 11pm," he said.

Title: Johnson & Johnson announces US$5.5bil settlement of talc lawsuits
Article:
NEW YORK: Johnson & Johnson said (J&J) on Monday it would pay US$5.5 billion to resolve tens of thousands of lawsuits alleging its baby powder and other talc products cause ovarian cancer, in a landmark settlement aimed at closing a chapter of contentious litigation that has dogged the company for years.
J&J said the settlement covers about 69,000 cases consolidated in federal court in New Jersey, and related cases in state court, totaling 99.75 per cent of the remaining talc claims.
Plaintiffs' law firms confirmed the deal on Monday, saying it was a good resolution after a decade-long court battle. The deal must still be approved by the judge overseeing the federal litigation.
J&J's vice president of litigation, Erik Haas, said the claims were "meritless" and that the company was willing to settle in order to get closure.
"While we are confident the company would have ultimately prevailed with further litigation, as it has in the vast majority of cases tried to date, this resolution allows the company to put this matter behind it and remain focused on its mission to develop medicines and devices that save lives," Haas said.
J&J won a significant court victory in the long-running legal battle last week, when a federal judge cast doubt on individual plaintiffs' ability to prove that talc specifically caused their ovarian cancer.
J&J has long denied that its talc products caused cancer, saying that talc was safe and did not contain asbestos. The company stopped selling talc-based baby powder in the US in 2020, switching to a cornstarch product.
The litigation resumed in March 2025, after being put on hold for more than three years during J&J's repeated failed attempts to resolve the lawsuits through a shell company's bankruptcy.
Unlike the proposed bankruptcy settlements, Monday's agreement applies only to existing claims and does not address future lawsuits.

Title: Chinese tech firms, from Apple suppliers to OpenAI rivals, raise US$27.13bil in Hong Kong
Article:
NEW YORK: From robotaxi developers to AI startups and chipmakers, Chinese technology firms are flocking to Hong Kong's booming capital markets, raising a combined HKUS$212.75 billion (US$27.13 billion) this year to fund expansion in AI, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing.
Here are some of the major companies that have recently listed or sold shares in the city:
CATL
The world's largest electric vehicle battery maker launched a roughly HKUS$39.2 billion (US$5.00 billion) share sale in April, less than a year after its blockbuster Hong Kong listing.
CATL, whose customers include Tesla, BMW, Volkswagen, Xiaomi and Nio, priced 62.4 million new H shares at HKUS$628.20 each.
Chaozhou Three-Circle
The electronic ceramic materials maker priced a share offering at the top end of its marketed range to raise about HKUS$7.16 billion.
Dajin Heavy Industry
In June, the wind power equipment maker set the offer price for its Hong Kong listing at HKUS$66.40 a share, aiming to raise HKUS$5.77 billion.
Shenzhen-listed Dajin said it plans to use 55 per cent of the proceeds to enhance deep-sea wind power services and 20 per cent to fund the construction of an assembly and operations facility in Europe.
GigaDevice Semiconductor
GigaDevice Semiconductor raised HKUS$4.68 billion in a Hong Kong listing in early January, with plans to use the proceeds for research and development as well as strategic and industry investment, including potential acquisitions.
Its shares soared almost 40 per cent in their Hong Kong trading debut on January 13.
Huaqin
The smart device maker raised HKUS$4.6 billion in a Hong Kong share offering in April.
The firm designs and manufactures electronic products for major technology brands, including smartphones, laptops, servers, smart home devices and wearables.
Its shares climbed 17 per cent in their Hong Kong debut.
Lingyi iTech
The Apple supplier priced its Hong Kong initial public offering to raise about HKUS$8.3 billion, seeking to use part of the proceeds to expand AI capacity.
Founded in 2006 by billionaire Zeng Fangqin, the company supplies parts for smartphones, tablets and laptop computers, and counts Huawei Technologies and Samsung Electronics among its customers.
MiniMax Group
MiniMax Group said it was seeking to raise HKUS$16.04 billion in fresh capital via a share sale and a bond issue to fund growth in its AI business.
It plans to raise about HKUS$9.54 billion by offering 35.6 million new Class A shares and the rest via zero-coupon bonds due 2027.
Earlier, the company raised HKUS$4.82 billion in its Hong Kong IPO in January.
MiniMax, founded in early 2022 by former SenseTime executive Yan Junjie, develops multimodal AI models that can generate text, audio, images, video and music.
Momenta Global
The Mercedes-Benz-backed robotaxi firm raised about HKUS$5.89 billion in a Hong Kong listing, though shares debuted flat amid caution around AI and other tech stocks.
Momenta, which provides assisted-driving solutions to automakers, including Toyota Motor and BYD, was founded in 2016 by former Microsoft researcher Cao Xudong.
Montage Technology
Montage Technology raised HKUS$7.04 billion in a share sale in February to fund research, commercialisation, strategic investment or acquisitions and working capital, its prospectus showed.
The semiconductor designer's offering attracted 17 cornerstone investors, including JPMorgan Asset Management, UBS Asset Management and Yunfeng Capital.
Founded in 2004, Montage designs integrated circuits that help speed data movement in servers and data centers.
Nexchip Semiconductor
The partially state-owned chipmaker priced an offering at the top end of its marketed range, aiming to raise around HKUS$6.98 billion.
The company plans to spend over HKUS$3.5 billion from the proceeds on research and development, and another HKUS$1.5 billion on AI-powered systems to integrate research, development and production processes.
OmniVision Integrated Circuits
OmniVision Integrated Circuits raised HKUS$4.80 billion in its Hong Kong listing in early January and plans to allocate about 70 per cent of the proceeds to research and development.
The firm is the third-largest digital image sensor provider globally, with a 13.7 per cent market share based on revenue from digital imaging solutions in 2024, it said in its Hong Kong listing prospectus, citing research and consultancy firm Frost & Sullivan.
Shanghai Biren Technology
AI chip startup Shanghai Biren Technology raised HKUS$5.58 billion in its Hong Kong listing in December, with most of the proceeds earmarked for research and development and commercialisation.
Founded in 2019, Biren's co-founders include Zhang Wen, formerly the president of AI face-recognition company SenseTime , and Jiao Guofang, who previously worked at Huawei and Qualcomm.
Shanghai Iluvatar CoreX Semiconductor
The Shanghai-headquartered firm launched a Hong Kong share sale aimed at raising around HKUS$7.07 billion.
GPU designer Iluvatar CoreX was offering 14.9 million new H shares at HKUS$476 apiece, representing a 15 per cent discount to the stock's last close.
The company said the proceeds from the share sale will be used to advance research and development, product iteration, and technology upgrades, among other uses.
Knowledge Atlas Technology JSC, known as Zhipu AI
Zhipu launched a HKUS$31.41 billion share sale in Hong Kong, showed a term sheet seen by Reuters.
The firm is one of China's best-known AI model developers and is viewed by investors as a fast-rising challenger to US firms such as OpenAI, helped by strong demand for large language models.
Zhongji Innolight
Chinese optical parts maker Zhongji Innolight set its Hong Kong listing price at HKUS$980 per H share, aiming to raise HKUS$53.41 billion in Asia's second-largest share sale this year.
The listing would also be Hong Kong's biggest share sale in nearly seven years, since Alibaba Group's US$12.9 billion listing in 2019, according to LSEG data.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 38 early voting centres for N9 polls opened at 8am
Article:
SEREMBAN: A total of 38 early voting centres for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election opened at 8 am today to allow 22,339 security forces personnel and their spouses to cast their ballots.
According to statistics from the Election Commission (EC), 16,884 members of the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) along with their spouses will cast their votes at eight designated polling centres.
The remaining 5,455 voters, consisting of members of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and their spouses, are scheduled to exercise their rights at 30 polling centres.
The polling centres will close in stages, according to the schedule set by the EC, between noon and 5 pm.
Meanwhile, checks by Bernama found that the weather in most areas was reported to be bright today.
This Saturday, approximately 889,490 ordinary voters will determine the mandate in the 36-seat Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly.
A total of 103 candidates are contesting the state polls, with Pakatan Harapan (PH) fielding the highest number of candidates at 36, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) (25) and Bersatu (24).
Perikatan Nasional (PN) is fielding 11 candidates, followed by four independent candidates, and one each from Barisan Jamaah Islamiah Semalaysia (Berjasa), Parti Orang Asli Malaysia (ASLI) and Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM).
The Negeri Sembilan State Assembly was dissolved on June 5 to pave the way for the state election, polling for which is on Aug 1. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three killed, toddler among four wounded in Seattle shooting
Article:
SEATTLE: A shooting near the Space Needle landmark in Seattle killed three people on Sunday and wounded at least four others including a toddler, officials said.
Seattle Police said one suspect was arrested and they were searching for another following the incident at a food festival in a popular tourist district of the northwestern US city.
Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said shots were heard around 6pm (0100 GMT) and "there were two people who we believe were shooting at each other." Two weapons were recovered.
There is "no outstanding threat to the community," he said.
Seattle Police said two people died at the scene at the Seattle Center and a third died in hospital.
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson said State Patrol SWAT officers had been deployed to assist local police.
"My prayers are with the families of the victims, and the responders as they work to keep people safe," he said on X.
Mayor Katie Wilson said the shooting was "an act of horrific violence."
"Our attention belongs to the people whose lives were taken, those fighting to recover, and the families beside them," she said in a statement.
Wilson also expressed her thanks to "the Seattle police officers who responded to the scene and took a suspect into custody."
Four patients were being treated at the trauma centre facility at Harborview Medical Center, according to spokesperson Susan Gregg: a child, a woman of unknown age who was in surgery, a 23-year-old man and a 39-year-old woman.
One of them did not survive their injuries, Davis said, without identifying the victim.
Another victim arrived later at the University of Washington Medical Center with a gunshot wound, according to Davis.
Those that remained in hospital, including the toddler, were in a "stable condition," he said.
Several witnesses told Seattle television station KIRO they heard multiple shots before running away.
"At first, I thought there were fireworks, and then everybody flooded and ran past us," Nick Bate told the station.
"We started running. I didn't know. I didn't look where the person was going. I just heard everything," a witness told AFP.
The shooting took place during the "Bite of Seattle" summer festival celebrating local businesses and food vendors.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Young voters weigh candidates' track records ahead of Negri Sembilan polls
Article:
SEREMBAN: A candidate's track record and background are among the key criteria young voters consider when choosing their representative.
Young voter K. Sasvini, 19, said she searched for information on candidates contesting the Sikamat state seat through the Election Commission's website.
"I also looked up the candidates' backgrounds and track records on social media and the internet to choose the right candidate.
"As a voter, I need to make sure I choose the right representative because the right choice will benefit the community in this area," she said.
Sasvini said she was excited to vote for the first time as she wanted to fulfil her responsibility of electing a representative for her constituency.
"I used to accompany my father to the polling station. This time, I have the opportunity to fulfil my responsibility as a voter.
"So, I'm excited to be voting for the first time," said the Form Six student at SMK Tunku Ampuan Durah here.
Another Form Six student from the same school, Amir Nur Afiq Zaidilah, 19, said he did not rely on information from the internet or social media when choosing a candidate.
"I think a lot of the information on the internet and social media is false. Because of that, I rely on my family members' views about the candidates.
"My family members know what is happening around them, including the assistance they have received and the facilities provided to the local community," he said.
He said he wanted a representative who could create job opportunities near his home in the Ampangan state constituency.
"As a young person, I see employment opportunities as an important issue that candidates should prioritise.
"As a local resident, I want job opportunities close to home without having to look for work elsewhere," he said.
Meanwhile, Nur Qairawani Asyura Mohamad Rosli, 19, said she wanted to vote for a candidate who was well known for regularly engaging with the local community.
"I want to choose a candidate I know because they frequently meet residents, actively participate in community programmes and contribute to the local community.
"That's why I decided to research the candidates contesting the Chembong state seat and also seek my parents' opinions," she said.
Qairawani said she was enthusiastic about voting for the first time because she would be doing so alongside five other members of her family.
"Besides my parents, my four siblings and I will also be voting at the same polling station.
"So, I'm excited not only because it is my first time voting, but also because I get to do it together with my family," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lax enforcement, coordination: Recurring floods expose Petaling Jaya's weaknesses [WATCH]
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Sivasangari Rama Rago buried her husband last August. And this year, three months apart, both on the 18th, both Saturdays, both around 4pm, she watched her two cars "die" in floodwaters in Taman Medan, Petaling Jaya.
She was inside her car the second time it flooded when a stranger pulled her out by the hand and said: "
Adik,
your life is more important than the car".
In Section 51A, Ibrahim Ali Hamzah has been running his family's drinks stall at Medan Selera 223 for 35 years.
The July 18th flood was his fourth experience this year; the water rose in 15 minutes flat.
Mixed-rice seller Jamaliah Yusoff, who has been doing business there for almost 40 years, said whenever it rains,  her heart pounds with the same fear she felt 15 years ago when traders had to climb  onto the roof beams to escape the rising water.
The
New Straits Times'
own site visit found drains "filled with rocks, sediment and overgrown shrubs", degraded from age and neglect.
This is not bad luck. It is the fourth flood this year at one food court, and the second car lost by one widow.
The real question isn't why Petaling Jaya floods — it's why, after decades of committees and press statements, it floods exactly the same way, every time.
A CITY OLD ENOUGH TO KNOW BETTER
Petaling Jaya is one of Malaysia's oldest planned townships.
Walk through any older section, Taman Medan, SS2, PJS estates, and try finding a drain in front of a house. You can't.
Decades ago, homeowners slabbed them over for porches and planter boxes, sealing them permanently.
Backyard drains fare no better, cleared only when a resident personally hounds the contractor, week after week, because nobody comes on schedule.
The Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) has admitted this itself.
Mayor Datuk Mohamad Zahri Samingon has acknowledged that permanently covered drains block maintenance access and notices would require owners to reopen them or fit inspection gaps.
Councillor Norah Mansor put it bluntly after the Taman Buana Perdana floods: "Enforcement must be strict".
If the council has known this for years, why are covered drains still choking hotspots in July 2026?
COUNCIL'S MATH DOESN'T ADD UP TO SAFETY
MBPJ isn't doing nothing. It has built retention ponds, river overflow control structures, flap gates and mobile pumps at hotspots like Taman Sri Manja and Jalan 223.
The state has just allocated RM40.5 million for 39 projects, eight prioritised.
But the mayor's own numbers expose the ceiling of this strategy: MBPJ's drains are designed for roughly 60mm of rain an hour, achieving 80 per cent effectiveness even with permanent pumps.
Recent storms blew past that —  138mm in a day, 79mm within one violent hour.
The council is fighting 21st-century climate with 20th-century drains, and only RM600,000 approved for a RM2 million pump request to the Housing and Local Government  Ministry.
Basic housekeeping compounds this.
NST found Section 51A drains clogged with debris "due to ageing and lack of maintenance".
Ibrahim was told a bridge was causing the floods; it was removed but the floods continued anyway.
"If removing the bridge wasn't the solution, then what is?" he asked — a question nobody has answered.
Worse, a warning siren meant to protect the food court malfunctioned on the  day it was needed. A siren that doesn't sound is worse than none, false comfort dressed up as preparedness.
CONCESSIONAIRES RARELY HELD ACCOUNTABLE
Drain desilting is contracted to waste concessionaires like KDEB Waste Management.
Councillors say they've "been cooperative and quick to respond", but cooperation isn't coverage, and responding after a flood isn't preventing one.
If contractors are paid to desilt on schedule, residents shouldn't have to chase them every time a backyard drain silts up.
MBPJ must publish cleaning schedules and logs, and attach real financial penalties, not warning letters, for missed cycles.
JPS AND THE JURISDICTION EXCUSE
Heavier river engineering sits with the Drainage and Irrigation Department (JPS), not MBPJ, a split that leaves residents bounced between agencies while their homes flood.
Even JPS' own contractors have caused floods: temporary sheet piles for a Sungai Penchala upgrade bottlenecked the river, flooding Jalan 223 twice in two weeks and submerging 60 stalls under 1.2m of water.
A project meant to reduce flooding caused it instead.
IT TAKES TWO TO TANGO
The uncomfortable truth is as such: The council alone cannot fix this, and residents who blame MBPJ for everything are lying to themselves.
Every drain sealed for a tidier porch, every plastic bag flicked into a monsoon drain, makes the next flood worse for the whole street.
MBPJ has said as much —  illegal dumping worsens flood risk and land owners must keep drains on their own lots clean.
Petaling Jaya needs, immediately:
A BINDING
by-law banning permanently sealed drain covers, enforced with  fines.
PUBLISHED,
auditable concessionaire cleaning schedules, cross-checked by residents' associations, with financial penalties for missed cycles.
ONE
named, accountable lead agency per hotspot, jointly binding MBPJ and JPS to a fixed public timeline.
FORMAL
community drain-adoption schemes through RAs and Rukun Tetangga.
ENFORCEABLE
uptime for sirens and sensors, with penalty clauses when they fail exactly when they are needed.
Sivasangari doesn't need a 39-project masterplan.
She needs the drain near her home to carry water away the next time it rains hard for an hour.
Ibrahim doesn't need another official photographing the same clogged drain; he needs to know, in writing, who is accountable  if his stall floods for the  fifth time.
Petaling Jaya isn't short of engineers or budgets.
It is short of enforcement, contractor accountability and citizens who would stop treating their own drain as somebody else's problem.
The council must lead with teeth, not task forces.
Concessionaires must be held to contract with penalties.
And every resident who has poured concrete over a drain must accept that they, too,  are why this city keeps drowning.
The water doesn't care whose jurisdiction it is under.
It's time everyone else stopped pretending they do, too.
The writer is the founding and past president of Bandar Sri Damansara Residents Association,  an LA 21 award winning township engineered through his leadership.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AMRO lifts Asean+3 growth forecast as AI demand boosts regional resilience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Asean+3 region's economic growth forecast has been revised upward to 4.1 per cent for 2026 from the previous projection of 4.0 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand, strong technology exports and sustained momentum in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector.
The Asean+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO), in its July 2026 Quarterly Update of the Asean+3 Regional Economic Outlook (AREO) released yesterday, said growth is expected to ease slightly to 4.0 per cent in 2027.
Headline inflation is now projected at 1.6 per cent in 2026, compared with the earlier forecast of 1.8 per cent, reflecting lower global commodity price assumptions.
AMRO said the region is on track to maintain solid growth in the first half of 2026, as robust AI-driven demand offsets headwinds from the prolonged Middle East conflict.
The upgraded outlook is supported by strong demand for semiconductors and other AI-related products, alongside a more favourable global commodity price environment.
Household spending has remained firm, supported by favourable labour market conditions and continued income growth, particularly in Asean economies, while investment has stayed resilient on the back of rising capital spending in advanced manufacturing and information and communication sectors.
Net exports have also continued to underpin growth, buoyed by strong semiconductor and electronics demand.
Meanwhile, disruptions to energy and industrial input supplies have proved less severe than initially feared, allowing manufacturing activity to continue expanding.
AMRO chief economist Dong He said the region had remained resilient, supported by firm domestic demand and its central role in global AI supply chains.
"The impact of the Middle East conflict has also been less severe than initially expected, although elevated energy and input costs continue to pose risks to inflation and industrial activity," he said during a virtual media briefing yesterday.
Inflationary pressures have remained broadly contained, with price increases largely concentrated in energy and transport, while core inflation has risen only modestly.
However, AMRO warned that food inflation could accelerate if higher production costs and adverse weather conditions are passed on to consumers.
Despite the stronger baseline outlook, the office cautioned that considerable uncertainties remain.
It said a renewed escalation of the Middle East conflict could drive up energy, shipping and food costs, while prolonged disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, with oil prices averaging between US$90 and US$100 per barrel through 2027, could slow regional growth to 2.8 per cent and push inflation to 4.6 per cent in 2027, the highest since the global financial crisis.
AMRO also identified the AI-driven technology cycle as a key downside risk.
AI-related products have accounted for more than two-thirds of the region's export growth over the past year, and a moderation in global technology investment could significantly weaken exports and business investment.
Under a scenario in which global technology investment slows to its 2024 pace, Asean+3 growth could ease to 3.7 per cent in 2026 and 2.5 per cent in 2027, marking the region's weakest expansion since the Asian Financial Crisis, excluding the pandemic years.
A disorderly correction in AI-related asset valuations could further amplify the slowdown through financial markets.
AMRO also warned that heightened volatility in global financial markets, driven by geopolitical tensions, elevated technology-sector valuations and uncertainty over the US monetary policy path, could trigger renewed capital flow volatility and tighten global financial conditions.
In addition, uncertainty over the replacement of the expired US global import surcharge, together with existing tariff measures, Section 301 investigations and the possible expansion of export controls and other non-tariff measures, could further disrupt regional supply chains, increase trade costs and dampen economic growth.
Dong He said the broad range of possible outcomes highlighted the need for policymakers to remain vigilant.
"Policymakers will need to respond flexibly to differing domestic conditions and rapidly evolving external risks, particularly the AI cycle and the Middle East conflict," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM58 billion growth push to support economic growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Economy Ministry seeks to allocate RM58 billion, or 70 per cent of the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) 2027 development expenditure, for basic development projects to ensure the continuity of ongoing initiatives, sustain economic growth momentum and accelerate national development amid a challenging global environment.
The proposal, which has yet to be submitted to the Finance Ministry for consideration under the 2027 budget, underscores the government's continued reliance on development spending to drive economic activity, create jobs and strengthen long-term productivity.
Basic development expenditure covers core public investments in physical infrastructure and essential services, including roads, schools, healthcare facilities, water supply, flood mitigation and other strategic projects. RP2, which comes under the Thirteenth Malaysia Plan, involves project screenings and budget examinations managed by the Ministry of Economy.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said maintaining a strong allocation for basic development would ensure the continuity of strategic projects, support regional development and accelerate the country's physical infrastructure.
Data from the Finance Ministry showed basic development expenditure amounted to RM57.6 billion, or 71 per cent of total development expenditure, in 2026, compared with RM55.67 billion, or 65 per cent, in 2025.
Akmal said project selection would continue to prioritise implementation readiness over ambition.
"We do not choose projects because they are easy to approve. We choose projects because they are ready to be implemented and capable of solving problems," he said during the Economy Ministry's monthly assembly in Putrajaya on Monday.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the proposed allocation suggests the government will maintain an expansionary fiscal stance, with development spending aimed at generating strong multiplier effects across the economy.
He told Business Times that increased spending on development projects will benefit contractors and vendors, which in turn supports employment, business activity and domestic economic growth.
Afzanizam expects basic infrastructure to remain the government's priority under the 2027 budget, particularly investments in schools, clinics, roads, flood mitigation projects and water infrastructure, as these projects deliver long-term economic and social benefits while addressing critical public needs.
Measured Spending
Sunway University economics professor Dr Oh Ei Sun said the projected development spending indicates the government is prioritising the completion of ongoing projects over launching new initiatives, given heightened global uncertainty.
"Launching new initiatives amidst global economic uncertainties would have been very risky," he told Business Times.
While describing the increase in development spending as modest, Oh said the 2027 budget should place greater emphasis on strengthening infrastructure and utilities, particularly energy, water supply and digital connectivity, to support future high-technology investments in Peninsular Malaysia while improving living standards in East Malaysia.
He said Malaysia's export-orientated economy remains vulnerable to external shocks despite its strong first-half growth.
"As Malaysia is an externally orientated trading economy, global uncertainties that could impact energy and food supplies, as well as disrupt global growth, would have direct impacts on Malaysia's growth."
On fiscal policy, he said the government would need to balance development spending with its fiscal consolidation objectives through a combination of new revenue measures and stronger governance.
"It may have to raise new taxes (which would impact business growth) and plug leakages (further anti-corruption efforts) to ensure development and maintenance needs," he said.
Oh, said development expenditure would only deliver stronger private investment and higher productivity if projects were aligned with industry needs and executed efficiently.
"Besides improving efficiency of project delivery and also reducing corruption and collusion, the development projects or incentives should be in line with what the private sector truly desires and is capable of absorbing and magnifying; else, they would end up as the latest examples of the already ubiquitous white elephants," he said.
Balanced Approach
Economist Geoffrey Williams said the projected allocation by the Economy Ministry reflects a prudent fiscal approach that balances development priorities with fiscal discipline.
He described the proposal as a conservative budget that prioritises the completion of existing projects rather than a major expansion in public spending.
"This is very conservative and focused on maintaining existing projects with only a minor increase from 2026. This is good because it reduces the need to borrow," he told Business Times.
Williams said the government's development strategy is increasingly shifting towards leveraging government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) through initiatives such as GEAR-uP (Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme) to support investment while reducing reliance on government borrowing.
"It maintains development expenditure but reduces reliance on tax and borrowing. This is a very good strategy. The sectors are mainly infrastructure and social sectors with commercial opportunities shifting to GEAR-uP and GLICS", he said.
Williams said Malaysia's stronger-than-expected economic performance in the first half of the year demonstrated the resilience of businesses despite global headwinds and expects growth to remain above Bank Negara's forecast range in the second half.
"Our forecast is for growth to remain strong in the second half of the year and exceed the 4.0 per cent to 5.0 per cent range of Bank Negara," he said.
"The government has taken a fiscal hit from the oil price hike. Without this, the fiscal position would be very strong from subsidy rationalisation."
"Nonetheless, the economy has been protected and consumers relatively unharmed because petrol and diesel prices have been maintained. This is excellent economic management. I don't normally use the term "excellent" but it really is excellent," he said.
Looking ahead to the 2027 budget, Williams said the government is likely to introduce more measures aimed at supporting household incomes ahead of the next general election.
He expects the budget to include higher allocations for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah programmes, the introduction of a non-contributory pension and additional initiatives to ease cost-of-living pressures amid stagnant wage growth.

Title: Iraq opens probe into Saudi drone attack claim
Article:
BAGHDAD: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on Monday for an investigation into Saudi Arabia's claim that drones targeting its territory had been launched by pro-Iran groups in Iraq, his spokesman said.
Zaidi directed "the competent security authorities to investigate the statement issued by the ministry of defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia regarding the targeting of the kingdom with drones launched from Iraqi territory", spokesman Sabah al-Numan said in a statement.
The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an umbrella network of Iran-backed Shia militias conducting attacks against US and Israeli targets while operating outside Iraq's formal military structure, said the Saudi accusations were "fabrications that serve only as an attempt to justify their inability to respond to the painful Yemeni strikes."
It warned Riyadh that any "foolish action" in Iraq will be met with a "tough" response.--AFP

Title: Trump touts economy, attacks Democrats in Michigan campaign-style speech
Article:
MILFORD, Michigan: US President Donald Trump touted his record on investment, job creation and tax cuts on Monday less than 100 days before the November elections, even as polls showed Americans increasingly souring on his handling of the economy.
In a campaign-style speech at a General Motors test facility in Michigan, Trump also lashed out at Democrats seeking to end Republican control of Congress, calling his political opponents "communists" to cheers from many in the audience.
"Jobs are up, inflation is down, our border is secure. Factories are opening at record levels. Investment is booming. Michigan is thriving. America is winning like never before," Trump said in a speech that also touched on immigration, the Iran war, voting restrictions and transgender issues.
Presidents often speak at auto plants but it is highly unusual for them to turn speeches at factories into campaign rallies. GM declined to comment on the partisan nature of Trump's speech.
The first 18 months of Trump's second term as president have featured a series of policy-driven economic shocks, driven by an immigration crackdown, higher tariffs and a war with Iran that has boosted the price of oil and ​threatened global supply chains.
Polls show that the high cost of living remains the top issue for American voters heading into the mid-term November elections, including in Michigan, a key swing state.
Trump's attacks on Democrats reflected a theme he has increasingly embraced in recent weeks. With the Iran war exacerbating Americans' economic concerns, he has sought to energise his political base by presenting Democrats as radicals bent on fundamentally transforming the country.
"We're having the single greatest year we've ever had as a country. We're not going to let these people destroy it," he told an audience that included GM CEO Mary Barra.
During the speech, Trump falsely claimed that Democrats seeking office wanted to raise taxes to 80 per cent and abolish the police. He also described the US trade deficit as having declined by 71 per cent, though the actual number in 2025 was a 0.2 per cent decline.
SKEPTICAL MICHIGAN
Michigan voters have become more skeptical about Trump's handling of the economy and trade, according to Bernie Porn, president and pollster at Epic MRA. Trump's job approval rating in the state has fallen to 33 per cent, with 61 per cent disapproving, while most voters say consumers — not foreign countries — are bearing the cost of tariffs.
"He's got a serious problem going into the midterms because people don't believe him and they don't think he's telling the truth," Porn said of the Republican president's problems in Michigan, where Epic MRA is based.
White House spokeswoman Liz Huston said Trump's "America First" agenda has driven automakers to invest, hire and expand, calling it a pace of growth "not seen in decades."
Trump defeated Democratic former Vice President Kamala Harris by roughly 1.4 percentage points in Michigan in the 2024 presidential election, flipping it back to Republicans after Democrat Joe Biden won the state in 2020.
Michigan will be a critical battleground in the fight for control of Congress, with an open Senate seat drawing national attention. The state's Republican and Democratic voters will choose their nominees in an August primary.
The Senate race will test whether Trump's strength among working-class voters can translate into broader political gains. Republicans are rallying behind former US congressman Mike Rogers, while Democrats are holding a competitive primary featuring US Representative Haley Stevens and former public health official Abdul El-Sayed.
Trump delivered his speech at GM's Milford Proving Ground, the company's vehicle-testing facility. Located about 40 miles (65 km) northwest of Detroit, the site covers thousands of acres and includes test tracks, laboratories and specialised facilities for simulating real-world driving conditions.
Trump has used tariffs to push American manufacturers to move production to the United States. GM plans to move production of the Chevrolet Blazer from Mexico, while adding Equinox production in the US to supplement existing capacity. --REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: N9 Polls: Early voters cast ballots today
Article:
SEREMBAN: A total of 22,339 military and police personnel and their spouses will cast their ballots today in the early voting for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election.
Of the total, 16,884 are military personnel and their spouses, while 5,455 are police personnel and their spouses.
All 38 polling centres will open at 8 am and will close in stages according to their respective locations, with 18 centres closing at noon, two at 2pm and the remaining at 5pm.
The centres include the Army Basic Training Centre (Pusasda) in Port Dickson, the Sendayan Air Base and the Negri Sembilan Police Contingent headquarters in Seremban, the Nilai Police headquarters, and Syed Sirajuddin Military Camp in Gemas, Tampin.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast fair weather across most areas of the state this morning, except in Port Dickson, where heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected, before heavy rain spreads to almost the entire state in the afternoon.
The state election will see contest for 36 seats, involving 103 candidates.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) is fielding candidates in all 36 seats, while Barisan Nasional (BN) is contesting 25 seats, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) 24, and Perikatan Nasional (PN) 11.
Also contesting are Barisan Jemaah Islamiah Se-Malaysia (Berjasa), Parti Orang Asli Malaysia (ASLI) and Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM), each fielding one candidate, as well as four Independents.
The 15th Negri Sembilan state election, held in 2023, saw PH win 17 of the 36 seats, followed by BN with 14 and PN with five.
The state legislative assembly was dissolved on June 5 to pave the way for the election. Polling is on Aug 1. — BERNAMA

Title: Foreigner in extortion case involving 12 cops held over passport offences
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR The foreigner who was allegedly extorted by 12 Kuala Lumpur policemen was arrested along with his two female accomplices from Thailand and China, police said.
The three were arrested under the Immigration Act on suspicion of travelling with false passports.
Also arrested were the 12 policemen who are being investigated for extortion, under Section 384 of the Penal Code.
They had their statements recorded and have been released on bail.
Police sources said the 30-year-old man, who claimed he was extorted, had been travelling on a Vanuatu passport but checks with the Chinese embassy confirmed he was also their citizen.
The Vanuatu consular-general in Kuala Lumpur, Henry Savarimuthu, told the
New Straits Times
the man had not approached the consulate for any help so far.
"If we grant a foreigner Vanuatu citizenship, it means our checks have found no criminal record against this person. I would be surprised if this person has any criminal history."
On Friday, police acting on a tip-off raided two upmarket condominium units in Kuala Lumpur and detained the man along with two women from Thailand and China.
They were suspected of operating a scam syndicate and taken to the Dang Wangi police headquarters for questioning.
Sources told the
NST
the policemen allegedly demanded RM2 million from the man, who managed to pay them about RM560,000.
He was released but came back the following day to lodge the extortion report before the 12 policemen were rounded up.
Sources said the case had  been taken over by the Criminal Investigation Department.
Savarimuthu said it was not surprising that the man had paid  RM560,000.
"Chinese nationals who obtain Vanuatu citizenships are generally wealthy and they often make payments using USDT (Tether cryptocurrency).
"When applying for Vanuatu citizenship, a single applicant pays US$130,000 (RM520,000)."
Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Sazalee Adam had confirmed the arrests of the 12 policemen, including a deputy superintendent and an assistant superintendent.
Meanwhile, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the arrests of the cops  showed that the force did  not compromise on misconduct.
He said the detention of the policemen sent a clear message that police would not tolerate any form of wrongdoing, including among its own members.
"The fact that the police arrested, detained and took action sends a clear message that the force will not tolerate this at all, even when it involves its own members," he said  after the Home Ministry's monthly assembly yesterday.

Title: Stability, change among key factors shaping Negri Sembilan election [WATCH]
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional has denied claims of any quarrel or disagreement with Perikatan Nasional, insisting that both coalitions continue to work together based on mutual understanding.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said differing views expressed previously were the result of varying circumstances in different states and should not be construed as a sign of a strained relationship.
"There is absolutely no quarrel, not even any difference of opinion. We are moving forward together based on mutual understanding. I have already refuted those statements because they were inappropriate.
"Perhaps what was said may be suitable for that particular state, but it is not appropriate for Negri Sembilan.
"Do not blame the media. The media merely reports what has been said… so far,  coverage has been good," he said after officiating at the Negri Sembilan Bumiputera entrepreneurs gathering here yesterday.
He was responding to Amanah and Bersatu leaders, who claimed the BN-PN understanding had failed to materialise due to alleged disputes.

Title: New Sirim certification to combat fake engine oils
Article:
The automotive aftermarket is facing an increasingly sophisticated threat, but Malaysian motorists now can protect their vehicles.
In a move against the proliferation of counterfeit engine oils, Sirim QAS International Sdn Bhd has officially rolled out the SIRIM 58 Standard — Certification Scheme for Genuine Products (Engine Oil for Motor Vehicles).
For years, counterfeit engine oils have posed a growing and complex challenge to consumers and the automotive industry. Today's counterfeiters no longer rely on easily identifiable, cheaply printed packaging. Instead, they produce highly sophisticated fakes that are nearly impossible to distinguish from genuine products through visual inspection alone.
The consequences of falling victim to these counterfeits are severe, with unknowing motorists risking mechanical damage, including drastically reduced vehicle performance, increased fuel consumption and premature engine wear.
Sirim QAS International Industrial, Consumer Certification and Inspection Section 2 head Hasnol Zakaria emphasised the critical need for this verification mechanism.
"While a counterfeit engine oil may cost less at the point of purchase, it could lead to significantly higher repair and maintenance costs for motorists in the long run.
"Through the Certification Scheme for Genuine Product, consumers have a trusted and convenient way to verify product authenticity before use."
However, the issue extends far beyond the individual consumer.
The availability of fake engine oils disrupts the entire automotive ecosystem, adversely affecting legitimate brand owners, distributors, retailers, workshops, service centres and commercial fleet operators who rely heavily on market integrity, product authenticity and consumer trust.
Recognising the severity of the issue, the Malaysian government, led by the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, has stepped up its enforcement efforts.
While the ministry has continuously tackled the issue under the Trademarks Act, the government took a significant step forward with the publication of the Trade Descriptions (Certification and Marking of Engine Oil for Motor Vehicle) Order in 2024.
In direct support of this strategic legislative move, Sirim QAS International was officially appointed as the competent authority.
Rising to the mandate, the agency introduced the Certification Scheme for Genuine Product, a proactive framework designed to prevent counterfeit engine oils from ever penetrating the Malaysian market.
The scheme is built on a robust foundation of independent third-party certification combined with cutting-edge digital security.
To prevent the system from being compromised by counterfeiters, the Sirim Conformity Label incorporates state-of-the-art technological features. This includes advanced digital security protocols that completely prevent the duplication or cloning of the label.
A key pillar of this initiative is consumer empowerment through the MySIRIM mobile application.
[[nid:1498470]]
It is available for free download on the Apple App Store, Google Play Store and Huawei AppGallery. The app transforms every smartphone into a powerful authentication tool.
Consumers are urged to look for the Sirim Conformity Label before making a purchase.
By scanning the label with the MySIRIM app, buyers can instantly verify the product's authenticity status. The app also displays specific product information, which consumers can cross-reference with the physical packaging.
This digital verification enables motorists to make informed purchasing decisions and effectively reject fake products.
As Malaysia's leading conformity assessment body, Sirim's role extends far beyond issuing security labels.
Backed by extensive technical expertise, the agency conducts assessments, verifies product traceability, and carries out ongoing monitoring and surveillance.
This strict oversight ensures that certified brands maintain certification integrity and compliance with all national regulations and standards.
Combating counterfeit products requires a comprehensive, whole-of-ecosystem approach involving the ministry, certification bodies, manufacturers, distributors, workshop operators and the public.
The Certification Scheme for Genuine Product serves as the linchpin of this collective effort, offering a trusted, unified mechanism for product authentication.
Motorists are also strongly encouraged to adopt safe purchasing habits.
They should purchase engine oil from authorised dealers and reputable retailers, actively look for the Sirim Conformity Label on product caps, and verify its authenticity via the MySIRIM app.
By choosing genuine, certified products, motorists can protect their automotive investments, support legitimate businesses, and strike a decisive blow against the counterfeit market.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Houthis pushing to model Iran's Hormuz control in Red Sea: Yemen
Article:
RIYADH: Yemen's Houthi Movement aims to replicate Iran's Hormuz Strait strategy in the Red Sea by disrupting shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb and has been emboldened by an insufficient international response, Yemen's top diplomat said on Monday.
"The Houthis want to copy the Iranian model and this will shut down two main straits, the gateways into the Gulf and Red Sea," Yemeni Foreign Minister-designate Afrah Al-Zouba said, speaking to a small group of journalists at the Yemeni embassy in the Saudi capital, Riyadh.
The Red Sea has become a new front in the Iran war, with the Houthis taking an escalatory approach against Saudi Arabia by firing missiles and drones at the kingdom and declaring a blockade on Saudi shipping.
Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes on what it said were Houthi military facilities and said it would protect commercial shipping, accusing the Houthis of serving foreign agendas.
The escalation has also threatened to bring back conflict to Yemen, where war killed hundreds of thousands of people after the Houthis stormed the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting Saudi Arabia to intervene at the head of an Arab coalition.
A truce was reached in 2022 but it has been pierced by the recent cross-border fire, and Saudi officials, Western diplomats and Yemeni officials see a return to full-scale war as more likely now than at any point since then.
Zouba said Yemen's government, which enjoys strong Saudi backing, was prepared for an escalation and that firing was taking place along the frontline, spanning the country's northwest from the Red Sea up to the Saudi border, but neither side had yet mounted an offensive.
"We think that this conflict now needs to come to an end, either via peaceful means, or the other way," she said.--REUTERS

Title: Four killed in Bentong crash covered by Perkeso's Lindung 24 Jam scheme
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Four of the six victims killed in Saturday's Jalan Karak Lama crash in Bentong have been confirmed eligible for benefits under the Social Security Organisation's (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam (24-Hour Protection) scheme.
Perkeso said the case underscored the importance of extending social security coverage beyond working hours.
Perkeso said V. Mugilan, A. Kanabati Raja, K. Alaganathan and M. Parathanman, aged between 16 and 25, were active contributors covered under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4).
Their families will each receive a RM3,000 funeral management benefit.
Mugilan's dependants are entitled to an invalidity pension of RM562.50, with his wife receiving payments for life and his 2-year-old child until the age of 21 or completion of a first degree.
Alaganathan's parents will receive RM564.36 for life, while his siblings will receive payments until they turn 21.
Kanabati Raja's family will receive monthly dependants' benefits of RM1,647, while Parathanman's dependants will receive RM891 a month. Perkeso said total dependants' benefits payable to the four families over 30 years would exceed RM900,000.
Three other victims had no active contribution records, while another had no contribution record, making them ineligible for benefits under Act 4.
Perkeso said the tragedy underscored the importance of Lindung 24 Jam, which came into effect on June 1 to provide coverage for contributors involved in accidents outside working hours.
"This 24-hour protection scheme safeguards the contributors' families, ensuring their survival, education and dignity remain protected."
Perkeso also revealed that the family of factory operator Muhammad Hafizi Muhammad Rizal, 22, became the first to receive dependants' benefits under Lindung 24 Jam when he was killed in a road accident in Merbok, Kedah, on June 12 while travelling to a friend's house after work.
Before the scheme's introduction, the accident would not have qualified for compensation because it occurred outside working hours.
His dependants will receive a RM3,000 funeral benefit and a monthly dependants' benefit of RM378.
Perkeso also approved claims under the scheme for two Penang contributors injured in accidents at home.
A 33-year-old man, who fractured his wrist after falling from a ladder while trimming a rambutan tree, received RM540 in temporary disablement benefit (TDB), while a RM1,000 implant was also approved.
A 49-year-old woman who suffered burns after being scalded by hot water at home received RM540 in TDB, with income replacement provided throughout her certified medical leave.  — BERNAMA

Title: NUTP backs use of military veterans as school wardens
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR:  The National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) supports the appointment of military veterans as full-time school wardens.
Its president, Aminuddin Awang, said the Education Ministry's biggest challenge was managing nearly 1,900 boarding schools nationwide.
"That is a good proposal and can be implemented at selected fully residential schools as a starting point.
"But it must be noted that there are only 58 Maktab Rendah Sains Mara (MRSM) hostels compared with the nearly 1,900 under the Education Ministry. The effectiveness of hostel management cannot be directly compared," he said yesterday.
He was commenting on Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki's proposal for the ministry to consider appointing military veterans as full-time wardens to curb bullying at boarding schools.
Aminuddin said NUTP had for years advocated appointing dedicated full-time wardens at all boarding schools.
"For NUTP, it does not matter whether they are veterans or non-veterans. What matters is having full-time wardens at boarding schools, especially fully residential schools.
"Hiring full-time wardens from outside the teaching force is a realistic step in curbing bullying and disciplinary misconduct while fostering student discipline."
The ministry reported in February that there were 2,889 bullying cases last year, comprising 740 in primary schools and 2,149 in secondary schools.
According to the Student Discipline System, there were 3,883 bullying cases reported in 2022,  6,528 in 2023 and 7,681 in 2024.

Title: Malaysia's rich shift into protection mode
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are  focused on building wealth buffers to offset inflation, according to the HSBC Affluent Investor Snapshot.
The survey found that high-net-worth individuals are adopting a "future-proofing mindset", prioritising long-term financial resilience.
Beyond building  wealth, investors are focused on preserving it and  preparing for retirement.
The survey showed that affluent and high-net-worth investors in Malaysia are moving cash more actively than their global peers.
Over the next 12 months, 16 per cent of Malaysian investors said they plan to reduce  cash holdings, above the  global average of 12 per cent.
Linda Yip, HSBC Malaysia country head of international wealth and premier banking,   said the   findings reflect the investment appetite of the bank's premier and premier elite clients.
"Affluent and high-net-worth individuals are strengthening their  wealth building and     rebalancing their portfolios to meet   financial goals.
"They are mindful of inflationary pressures and the need to build retirement buffers."
The survey showed the top three  products held  by affluent and high-net-worth investors  are insurance (48 per cent), stocks (44 per cent) and gold (43 per cent).
Yip added that investors  continue to seek long-term growth, with product choices  becoming more targeted.
"While portfolios remain anchored in traditional products such as insurance and stocks,  investors   are also  adding    alternative assets alongside   gold and term deposits."
The survey polled close to 10,000 affluent and high-net-worth individuals  in 10 markets, including Malaysia.

Title: Trump sees Iran deal despite fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia
Article:
TEHERAN: US President Donald Trump on Monday voiced optimism at the prospects for a negotiated peace deal with Iran, as the two sides held their fire for a third consecutive day.
Fighting between the longtime foes has been paused since Friday after 13 nights of renewed US strikes on the Islamic republic sparked by a breakdown in diplomacy over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
But the US leader expressed hope that renewed diplomacy could bring an end to the war that began in late February with a wave of US-Israeli strikes, rattling both the region and the global economy.
"I have a lot of patience... We'll see what happens," he said aboard Air Force One. "I think there is a good chance that something could happen."
Teheran had earlier denied that there were any talks with the US to end the conflict.
"Mediators may convey messages from the American side to us regarding current developments in the region. But at present, we are not engaged in any negotiations with the United States," said Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.
But Trump insisted during a speech in Michigan that "right now, they're talking to us about making a deal."
Aboard Air Force One, the US president had earlier said that if the new efforts failed, "we go back to doing what we were doing" before the pause in fighting.
On that subject, he dismissed concerns that US ammunition stockpiles were running low nearly five months after the war began.
"We have a lot of ammunition. We have a lot of the mid-level stuff too, more than we could ever use no matter what," he said.
- SAUDI ARABIA ATTACKED -
Despite the recent lull, Saudi Arabia came under attack on Monday, with its defence ministry saying it had intercepted several drones fired by Iran-linked groups in Iraq targeting oil facilities.
No group claimed responsibility, but Riyadh called on Baghdad to prevent such attacks from being launched from its territory.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi later called for an investigation into Saudi Arabia's allegations.
Pakistan, which has been mediating a resolution to the Middle East war, condemned the drone attacks, saying they "pose a grave threat to peace and stability" in the Middle East.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels also said they launched drone attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure in response to incursions by the kingdom's drones. Riyadh is yet to comment on the claim.
Saudi Arabia and other Gulf nations accused pro-Iran militias in Iraq of launching waves of attacks on their territory during the conflict's earlier phase, but the groups have not claimed any attacks in the region since the resumption of hostilities.
Elsewhere, the Israeli military, which has not joined the recent fighting, said it had intercepted two drones near the Jordanian border and was investigating where they had been launched from.
Global stock markets meanwhile rallied and oil prices tumbled on Monday after the pause in strikes between Washington and Teheran.
It came as respite for Gulf shipping and the oil industry, with international benchmark Brent dropping six percent to around US$86 a barrel.
- 'MAFIA GANG' -
Control of the Strait of Hormuz remains a hurdle to any peaceful resolution, and Iran insists on managing the crucial conduit for oil and gas.
Its powerful Revolutionary Guards have been stopping vessels trying to transit the trade route in recent days, including six that state television on Monday said had sailed outside Iran's designated route.
Teheran says it has held talks in recent days with Oman, which also borders the strait, on "common principles and operational mechanisms" to ensure the safe passage of shipping.
In June, Muscat and Teheran said they would discuss imposing service fees, a move Washington opposes.
But Oman also angered Iran after saying vessels could transit the Hormuz strait via its waters, with Teheran responding by attacking ships.
Baqaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman, on Monday said the United States was not involved in the recent discussions with Oman.
Instead he criticised Washington, saying its conduct in recent years has "resembled that of a mafia gang that adheres to no rules or laws." --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Yemen prepared for any escalations with Houthis
Article:
RIYADH: Yemen's internationally recognised government on Monday said it is ready for any escalation with Houthi rebels after the Iran-backed group launched attacks and a maritime blockade targeting Saudi Arabia.
Fears are growing that renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels in Yemen may further destabilise the Arabian peninsula and rattle the region's precarious fault lines.
"At the end of the day, we are prepared for any escalations," Yemen's foreign minister designate Afrah al-Zouba told reporters during a briefing in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
The comments came just hours after the Houthis said they launched fresh drone strikes targeting Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure in response to incursions by the kingdom's drones.
Al-Zouba said the government was increasingly worried that the Tehran-backed rebels were copying Iranian manoeuvres in the Strait of Hormuz to gain control over the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a crucial passage into the Red Sea off the Yemeni coast.
The narrow waterway has been a critical artery for delivering vast quantities of Saudi crude to the international market, after maritime traffic was largely choked off by fighting in the Strait of Hormuz.
Last week, the Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and have claimed attacks targeting Saudi tankers and oil infrastructure in the kingdom.
The "Houthis want to copy the Iran experience in Hormuz," al-Zouba said, adding the rebels were "in harmony" with Iranian escalation in the region.
"They think they will gain control over the Red Sea," she added.
Al-Zouba said the situation in Yemen was tense with Houthi forces skirmishing with government troops in several areas across the country daily.
A Saudi-led military coalition had fought against the Houthi rebels in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government after war broke out in the country in 2015.
The latest flare-up between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis marks the first time in years the two sides have traded blows, threatening a 2022 truce in the previous conflict that has held despite expiring.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man claiming police extorted him wanted by Interpol over scam case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A foreigner who lodged a police report alleging he was extorted by individuals believed to be the police is now under investigation after checks with the International Criminal Police Organisation (Interpol) found he was wanted in China over a fraud case.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said checks revealed that the man was not a Vanuatu national as initially claimed, but was believed to be a Chinese citizen.
"Checks through Interpol found that the complainant is a Chinese national who is wanted in China for fraud.
"There are also doubts over the passport submitted by the complainant. The passport states that he was born in Pontianak, Indonesia, whereas Interpol records show his place of birth is China," he said in a statement.
Fadil said police received the report at 2.38am on July 24 over allegations of extortion involving the foreigner and two women, both aged 30.
The complainant alleged that a group of between 12 and 15 people, including a woman, entered his condominium unit in Jalan Ampang.
He claimed the group identified themselves as police officers before taking him and his two female companions to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters.
"Upon arriving at the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters, two individuals who claimed to be police officers instructed the complainant to transfer money into a bank account provided to avoid being detained.
"Fearing arrest, the complainant transferred the money into the account. He and his two companions were then released," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 384 of the Penal Code for extortion. Following the report, police arrested 15 police officers believed to be linked to the case.
"All those arrested have since been released on police bail after the initial investigation procedures were completed," he said.
Based on information obtained during the investigation, Fadil said police later arrested the complainant, a Chinese woman and a Thai woman about 1.30am yesterday.
He said they are being investigated under Section 12(1)(b) of the Passports Act 1966, as well as Sections 6(1)(c) and 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for offences related to travel documents and immigration.
However, Fadil said the Thai national was released after checks by the Immigration Department confirmed that her travel documents were valid.
"A 14-day remand order, from yesterday until Aug 9, has been obtained for the complainant and his companion, a Chinese national, to facilitate further investigations.
"The case remains under investigation and will be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further instructions," he said.
Fadil also advised the public against speculating on the case, as doing so could interfere with the investigation.
It was previously reported that Bukit Aman's Integrity and Standards Compliance Department had opened a disciplinary investigation into 12 police officers suspected of involvement in the alleged extortion of a man initially believed to be a Vanuatu national involving RM2 million.
Its director, Datuk Aida Abdul Hamid, said the disciplinary probe was opened in tandem with the criminal investigation being conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department.
Police had earlier arrested 12 officers of various ranks on suspicion of extorting RM2 million from the man. According to a source, the victim was released only after paying US$140,000 (RM560,000).

Title: El Nino: Johor, Melaka face up to 40 per cent less rainfall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor and Melaka are expected to record a reduction of between 20 and 40 per cent in rainfall when the country enters the Northeast Monsoon season at the end of the year due to the El Nino phenomenon.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the east coast of Sabah could also experience reduced rainfall due to its location closer to the Pacific Ocean.
However, he said states along the east coast and northern parts of the Peninsula were not expected to experience significant effects until the end of the year, based on six-month projections.
"Based on the information we have and rainfall projections six months ahead, we do not see significant effects on the east coast until the end of the year," he said as a guest on Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme titled El Nino: Is Malaysia Ready? yesterday.
Hisham said the Northeast Monsoon typically begins in late October or early November and ends in late March, with east coast states usually receiving the highest rainfall in November and December.
He said the effects of El Nino were expected to become more pronounced towards the end of the Northeast Monsoon before reaching their peak in early 2027.
He added that temperatures exceeding 35 degrees Celsius could occur between February and May, and possibly extend into June.
According to him, areas that typically experience high temperatures during very strong El Nino episodes include Perlis, Kedah, northern Perak, inland areas of Kelantan and parts of inland Pahang.
Meanwhile, Hisham said analysis of Malaysia's temperatures since the 1980s showed an increase of 0.19 degrees Celsius per decade due to global warming, while a strong El Niño could raise temperatures by up to 0.7 degrees Celsius above normal.
"If this El Nino reaches the very strong level that is expected, the country's highest temperature could surpass the record of 40.1 degrees Celsius recorded on April 9, 1998, with a potential temperature surge occurring between March and May 2027," he said.
He said reduced rainfall and rising temperatures could affect agricultural and livestock production, lower water levels in reservoirs and dams, and increase the risk of forest fires and transboundary haze.
To mitigate the impact of dry weather, Hisham said MetMalaysia provides technical advice to support cloud-seeding operations aimed at increasing water levels in catchment areas, although such operations can only be carried out when weather conditions are suitable.
"El Nino cannot be controlled because it is a natural phenomenon. What we at MetMalaysia can do is provide information on the conditions that are expected to occur," he said.
He also advised the public to use water wisely and avoid open burning to reduce risks during hot and dry weather. — BERNAMA

Title: Four trucks take hundreds of Rohingya from UNHCR office to KL police HQ
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hundreds of Rohingya refugees who gathered outside the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Jalan Bukit Petaling here yesterday were moved to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters for documentation and identity verification.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus, when contacted, confirmed that all the foreign nationals had been transferred to the police headquarters.
Checks at the scene found that the transfer operation began at 8.20pm, using four police trucks after the two vehicles initially deployed proved insufficient as many of the refugees were carrying luggage and personal belongings.
The refugees are understood to be undergoing identity checks before further action is taken by the relevant authorities.
Meanwhile, a source said the National Security Council is expected to coordinate the case today to identify refugees holding valid UNHCR documents and determine suitable placement for them.
According to the source, individuals without UNHCR cards or those unable to prove their legitimate refugee status will be handed over to the Immigration Department before being sent to an immigration depot pending repatriation to their countries of origin.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday said the government would not compromise with any refugee group that disrupts public order or attempts to take control of any area in the country.
He said enforcement agencies, including the police, Immigration Department and local authorities, had been instructed to take firm action against anyone found violating the law.
The media previously reported that the refugee group arrived in the capital yesterday on three buses after relocating from their settlement in Penang.
